Cooling

AC repair

The most common call. The system runs but blows warm air, the outdoor unit hums and will not start, ice forms on the copper lines, or water shows up where it should not. A good technician measures before replacing parts, names what failed and prices the fix before starting.

Emergency AC repair

The same work after hours, when heat is a health risk. That page covers who is most at risk in a Dallas heat wave, what to do while you wait, cooling centers, and how after-hours charges usually work.

AC installation and replacement

When repair no longer makes sense. Sizing with a load calculation, efficiency ratings, the newer refrigerants, permits and what a complete written quote should list.

Heating

Furnace and heating repair

Gas furnaces, heat pumps and electric heat strips each fail in their own ways. The page starts with gas and carbon monoxide safety, then explains what a technician checks when the heat will not come on, and why a hard freeze like February 2021 tests systems that rarely work hard in a Dallas winter.

HVAC tune-up and maintenance

A spring check before cooling season and a fall check before heating season. The page lists what a real tune-up includes, what it does not, and the filter and drain habits that prevent most problems.

Choosing who does the work

Whatever the service, the company you are put through to is independent of the line. Before you approve any work, read the guide to choosing an HVAC company in Dallas, and check the license yourself.

Check the license yourself. In Texas, air conditioning and refrigeration contractors are licensed by the Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation (TDLR), and the license number belongs on the company's quotes and invoices. Ask for it and look it up with the TDLR license search (opens in a new tab) before work starts. It is also fair to ask for a certificate of insurance.

Common questions

What is the difference between an HVAC tune-up and an AC repair?

A tune-up is planned maintenance on a system that works: cleaning, measuring and checking parts before they fail. A repair fixes something that has already stopped working or is working badly. If the system is blowing warm air or not running, you need a repair visit, not a tune-up. See AC repair and HVAC tune-up.

Should I repair or replace my air conditioner?

It depends on the system's age, its condition and what the repair costs. A working system does not have to be replaced because of the refrigerant rule changes. Ask the company to name the failed part and price the repair before you talk replacement. The AC installation page covers the decision in detail.

Does the line handle heating calls too?

Yes. Calls about furnaces, heat pumps and electric heat go through the same way: the automated assistant asks whether it is cooling or heating and transfers you to a local company. If you smell gas, leave the house first and call 911 and your gas utility from outside. See furnace and heating repair.

Can businesses use the line?

Yes. Offices, shops, restaurants and other businesses can call about rooftop units and commercial systems. The call is transferred the same way, to an independent company. See commercial HVAC.

Does Dallas Air & Heating do any of this work itself?

No. It is a free phone line. It transfers your call to an independent, locally owned heating and air conditioning company, and that company diagnoses the problem, quotes its own price and does the work. See how it works.
